episodes.title: The Number Twice Sold
episodes.script:
SFX: Champagne glasses clink. A sheet of bond paper snaps open.

MILES: This border is crooked. I want the certificate replaced before anyone sees it.

EWAN: Give it to me, please. I can correct the impression.

BELL: Correct it? You printed it.

SFX: Conversations fall quiet, one by one.

EWAN: I copied the register entry. The printing was done elsewhere.

BELL: Let us be exact. My guests did not purchase excuses from elsewhere. They purchased a Ravenshore bond from this office.

MILES: Two hundred pounds, Uncle. For two hundred pounds, the palm trees ought to stand straight.

SFX: Scattered laughter.

EWAN: The engraving is ornamental. The bond remains valid.

BELL: You hear that, gentlemen? Our provincial clerk has declared it valid. Perhaps the Bank of England may now rest.

INVESTOR: Does the clerk also govern Ravenshore?

MILES: No. He governs the ink.

SFX: Louder laughter.

EWAN: If you please, the date, denomination and signature are correct.

BELL: And yet the border has shifted, the lower seal is blurred, and the word treasury has lost a letter.

EWAN: That plate did not leave my desk in that condition.

BELL: Careful. A man may survive poor work. He rarely survives blaming his betters for it.

SFX: A ceremonial sword taps against a chair. The room settles.

MACRAE: Friends, Ravenshore is larger than one clerk's error.

MILES: Thank heaven for that.

MACRAE: Its forests stand untouched. Its rivers carry wealth to the sea. Every acre subscribed tonight brings roads, harbours and honest employment to a young nation.

INVESTOR: And the interest?

MACRAE: Six per cent, paid by a treasury whose future revenue rests on millions of fertile acres.

SFX: Applause rises around the room.

MACRAE: Mr Bell gave London the opportunity. You, gentlemen, give Ravenshore prosperity.

BELL: And Macrae gives it a sovereign's honour.

SFX: Glasses raised. Applause grows.

NARRATOR: Ewan stood beside the refreshment table holding the crooked certificate. He was ashamed, and everyone in the salon knew it.

MILES: Kerr, since you are idle, fetch me another bond.

EWAN: I have been dismissed from the table.

MILES: Then you have time.

BELL: Take the spoiled sheet downstairs. You will not copy another certificate tonight.

EWAN: Mr Bell, the impression was damaged after it left my desk.

BELL: You are a junior clerk from a town my guests could not find on a map. Macrae has raised twenty-three thousand pounds in subscriptions. Which fact shall command the room?

EWAN: The true one.

SFX: A short, embarrassed silence. Someone coughs.

BELL: Your wages are twelve shillings a week. Do not spend all twelve on principles.

MACRAE: Bell, be kind. A nervous clerk can still become a useful clerk.

EWAN: I am not nervous.

MACRAE: Then learn the difference between being correct and being believed.

SFX: Another burst of applause calls Macrae away.

BELL: Downstairs, Kerr.

SFX: Door closes. Applause muffles. Footsteps descend narrow wooden stairs.

NARRATOR: Below the salon, belief was stored in drawers: bonds, receipts, maps and seals. Ewan knew every drawer because he had copied every label.

SFX: Desk drawer slides open. Papers shuffle quickly.

EWAN: Ravenshore national loan. Two hundred pounds. Issue three.

SFX: Pencil scratches.

EWAN: Plate mark seven. Lower seal blurred after pressing.

SFX: Another drawer opens.

PIPPA: You were told not to copy another certificate.

EWAN: I am recording why this one is not mine.

PIPPA: Bell will call that disobedience with unusually neat handwriting.

EWAN: Look at the paper. The embossing is crushed over the wet ink. Someone stacked it before it dried.

PIPPA: That clears the printer. It does not clear you.

EWAN: The serial will.

SFX: Bond lifted close to a gas flame.

EWAN: R-four-one-eight-seven.

PIPPA: That is not in tonight's subscription list.

EWAN: Then Miles was given an older sheet.

PIPPA: Or an unentered one.

EWAN: Bring the paid receipts.

PIPPA: Bell keeps those in his private drawer.

EWAN: You have the counterfoils.

SFX: Pippa unlocks a small cash box. Thick paper flicks past under her thumb.

PIPPA: Four-one-eight-three. Four-one-eight-four. Four-one-eight-five.

EWAN: Keep going.

PIPPA: Four-one-eight-six.

SFX: Paper stops.

EWAN: Read the next one.

PIPPA: Paid in full. Two hundred pounds. Assigned to a Bristol subscriber three weeks ago.

EWAN: The serial?

PIPPA: R-four-one-eight-seven.

SFX: The salon applauds Macrae overhead.

EWAN: The bond I was accused of misprinting carries a serial number already sold to a different investor.

episodes.title: Behind the Counting-Room Door
episodes.script:
SFX: A ledger thumps onto a desk. A key turns in the outer office door.

EWAN: R-four-one-eight-seven was sold twice. Open Bell's private ledger.

PIPPA: Lower your voice.

EWAN: I want the entry before he destroys it.

PIPPA: And I want employment tomorrow morning.

EWAN: A subscriber paid two hundred pounds for a number now printed on Miles's bond.

PIPPA: I can count, Ewan.

EWAN: Then help me prove it was not a copying error.

PIPPA: Bell's drawer has two locks. I have one key.

EWAN: Who has the other?

SFX: A walking cane strikes the floor behind them.

BELL: The man whose private drawer you are discussing.

SFX: Nothing. Long.

BELL: Miss Shaw, upstairs. Kerr, remain.

PIPPA: Mr Bell, the counterfoil—

BELL: Upstairs.

SFX: Pippa's footsteps retreat. Door closes.

BELL: Let us be exact. You were dismissed from the salon table. You entered the accounts room. You opened paid subscription records.

EWAN: I found a duplicated serial.

BELL: You found paperwork beyond your station.

EWAN: The same bond number has taken four hundred pounds from two investors.

BELL: Has either investor complained?

EWAN: They do not know.

BELL: Then at present the only injury is to your sleep.

EWAN: Open your ledger.

BELL: That was almost an order.

EWAN: Open it, please.

BELL: Better.

SFX: Two keys enter two locks. A heavy drawer rolls out.

BELL: You may inspect the page. You may not touch it.

SFX: Ledger cover creaks.

EWAN: Issue three. Subscriptions received.

BELL: Read silently.

EWAN: R-four-one-eight-seven. Two hundred pounds. Bristol account.

SFX: Page turns.

EWAN: R-four-one-eight-seven again. Two hundred pounds. Miles Orrock.

BELL: A repetition.

EWAN: In different ink, entered eleven days apart.

BELL: Still a repetition.

EWAN: Your private ledger confirms both payments.

BELL: It confirms that two lines exist.

EWAN: One certificate number cannot secure two debts.

BELL: Ravenshore contains eight million acres. I think it can survive one overworked numeral.

EWAN: It is fraud if it was deliberate.

BELL: Such an ugly word from a man asking me for wages.

EWAN: I am asking you to cancel Miles's bond and return the second payment.

BELL: No.

EWAN: Then I will tell him.

BELL: Your mother's house is still burdened by your father's creditors, is it not.

EWAN: Leave her out of this.

BELL: I am trying to help. A dismissed clerk finds family obligations terribly expensive.

EWAN: That is a threat.

BELL: It is arithmetic.

SFX: Bell closes the private ledger.

BELL: We have a more immediate difficulty. Yesterday's bond register is unreadable.

SFX: Wet, swollen pages slap onto the desk.

EWAN: Water damage.

BELL: A porter upset a pail. You will recreate every entry from the counterfoils before morning.

EWAN: There are three hundred and twelve certificates.

BELL: Then your handwriting will finally justify its salary.

EWAN: I will not alter the duplicate.

BELL: Copy what the records say.

EWAN: The records say you accepted two payments against one number.

BELL: And if the register is not complete by eight, the records will say you abandoned your post after damaging it.

SFX: Bell walks to the door.

EWAN: You cannot keep me here.

BELL: The silver must be protected overnight. Surely you understand.

SFX: Door closes. Key turns from the outside.

EWAN: Bell!

SFX: Ewan pounds the locked door.

BELL: Through the door, Kerr. Three hundred and twelve entries. Do be accurate.

SFX: Bell's footsteps fade.

NARRATOR: Ewan wanted the truth entered once. Bell required the lie copied three hundred and twelve times.

SFX: Clock ticks. Pen scratches rapidly. Pages turn.

EWAN: R-four-one-seven-nine. One hundred pounds. R-four-one-eight-zero. Two hundred pounds.

SFX: Pen scratches. Clock continues.

EWAN: R-four-one-eight-seven. Bristol account. Two hundred pounds.

SFX: Pen pauses.

EWAN: R-four-one-eight-seven. Miles Orrock. Two hundred pounds.

SFX: Ewan draws a hard line beneath both entries.

EWAN: Duplicate serial retained exactly as found.

SFX: A folded paper slides under the locked door.

EWAN: Pippa?

PIPPA: Quietly.

EWAN: Bell has the key.

PIPPA: I know. I also know what left the office while you were in the salon.

EWAN: What is this docket?

PIPPA: Freight received at half past six. Six sealed cases.

EWAN: Destination: Alderwick Auction Rooms.

PIPPA: Bell's first public sale begins tomorrow.

EWAN: This says eight hundred certificates. The authentication column is signed E.K.

PIPPA: Those are not your strokes.

EWAN: I signed none of them.

PIPPA: A fresh shipment of Ravenshore bonds has already been sent to the auction house.

EWAN: And every certificate carries my forged initials.

episodes.title: The Clerk on the Platform
episodes.script:
SFX: A meeting-hall door bangs open. Boots stamp on bare boards. A handbell rings over a crowded room.

MARA: You are late, Ewan. Get on the platform.

EWAN: I need five minutes alone with you.

MARA: You need to stand beside me and answer questions.

EWAN: About a country I have never seen?

MARA: Names first, doubts later. Up you go.

SFX: Mara pulls him up two wooden steps. The handbell rings again.

NARRATOR: Seven days after Bell locked the counting room, Ewan was sent north with a case of maps and a warning to be useful.

MARA: Families of Calderwick, thank you. Tonight we take final deposits for land and passage to Ravenshore.

SFX: Chairs scrape. Excited murmurs fill the hall.

MARA: You have heard promises from travellers and agents. Now you may question a government clerk from the London treasury itself.

EWAN: I am a copying clerk.

MARA: Mr Ewan Kerr prepares the official bonds, registers and land grants.

VOICE IN HALL: Is he a treasury man or not?

MARA: He works inside the Ravenshore office. Ask him anything.

SFX: Several voices call at once.

AGNES: Wages first.

MARA: Mrs Murray has the floor.

AGNES: My eldest is a wheelwright. The notice says skilled men earn four shillings a day. Is that guaranteed?

EWAN: The printed schedule states four shillings.

AGNES: I asked whether it is guaranteed.

MARA: The land company requires roads, carts and mills. A wheelwright will not lack work.

AGNES: Let the clerk answer.

SFX: The room quiets.

EWAN: I have seen no signed wage contract.

VOICE IN HALL: Then what good are the notices?

MARA: Names first, doubts later. Mr Kerr means wages depend upon trade, as wages do here.

AGNES: Here, I know who pays them.

EWAN: That is a fair question.

MARA: And Ravenshore has a fair answer. New settlements pay the men who build them.

THOMAS: What has already been built?

MARA: Your name?

THOMAS: Thomas Hale. Surveyor.

MARA: Mr Hale, the capital has government offices, a bank, a cathedral square and planned streets running from the harbour.

THOMAS: Has the clerk seen those streets?

EWAN: No.

SFX: Murmurs sharpen.

THOMAS: The harbour?

EWAN: No.

THOMAS: The bank?

EWAN: I have seen its charter.

THOMAS: Paper.

EWAN: Yes.

VOICE IN HALL: He has never been there!

ANOTHER VOICE: They brought us a clerk who has never seen the place!

SFX: A few people laugh. Someone knocks a cane against the floor.

MARA: A London clerk does not inspect every acre governed by his office.

THOMAS: How many acres have been surveyed?

EWAN: The land schedule lists one hundred and fifty thousand available for first settlement.

THOMAS: That was not my question.

EWAN: I have not seen a completed survey.

MARA: Which is why Ravenshore is recruiting surveyors. Mr Hale has just explained his own opportunity.

SFX: Laughter breaks the tension.

MARA: Farms begin at thirty acres. Skilled families may claim sixty. Deposits are five pounds, with passage charged separately by berth.

AGNES: My family shop sold for eighty-six pounds. That is all we possess.

MARA: In Scotland, eighty-six pounds purchases another year of rent and worry. In Ravenshore, it purchases land.

AGNES: I have two children.

MARA: Then purchase two futures.

EWAN: Mrs Murray, do not pay tonight.

SFX: The room reacts with a low gasp.

MARA: Mr Kerr is concerned that you choose the correct acreage.

EWAN: I am concerned she has sold her shop.

AGNES: You heard her. Thirty acres begins at five pounds.

EWAN: A deposit is not land.

MARA: It secures land.

EWAN: Only if the grant can be honoured.

MARA: The grants carry Macrae's seal, Bell's bank certification and your office registration.

AGNES: Is that true?

EWAN: Those marks are on the documents.

AGNES: And you enter them in the register?

EWAN: I have entered land grants, yes.

AGNES: Then my family's claim will be written where nobody can deny it.

EWAN: A written claim is not the same as possession.

MARA: He is a clerk. To him, nothing exists until it has three copies and a ribbon.

SFX: The room laughs again, this time warmly.

AGNES: I will pay five pounds for the land and twelve for three berths.

SFX: Coins spill onto a table.

EWAN: Wait.

MARA: Deposit received from the Murray family. Seventeen pounds.

SFX: Applause. More chairs scrape as people rise.

VOICE IN HALL: Put me down for thirty acres.

ANOTHER VOICE: Two berths here.

VOICE NEAR TABLE: I have ten pounds now and the rest at the dock.

SFX: Coins, pens and overlapping voices build into a rush.

EWAN: Mara, stop taking money.

MARA: I have spent four months bringing these families to this table.

EWAN: Bell's bonds carry duplicate numbers.

MARA: Not here.

EWAN: My initials were forged on the latest shipment.

MARA: Not here.

EWAN: They deserve to know what the London office is doing.

MARA: And do you know what awaits them here? Rent, debt and sons working another man's field. Do not mistake uncertainty for cruelty.

EWAN: You promised a capital city.

MARA: Macrae promised it. Bell financed it. You put it into respectable handwriting.

EWAN: I copied what I was given.

MARA: So did I.

SFX: A ledger page turns. Mara writes quickly.

AGNES: Mr Kerr, come witness my entry.

EWAN: I cannot.

AGNES: You told us you keep the register.

EWAN: I said I copied it.

AGNES: Then copy my name correctly. Murray. Three berths. Thirty acres.

SFX: Pen is pressed into Ewan's hand.

MARA: Names first, doubts later.

SFX: Ewan writes one line. The pen scratches loudly beneath the crowd.

EWAN: Agnes Murray. Deposit, seventeen pounds.

AGNES: Thank you, Mr Kerr. My children will know who witnessed it.

NARRATOR: That gratitude cost Ewan more than the public laughter. Agnes trusted him because his handwriting looked like authority.

SFX: Meeting hall empties. Coins are counted into stacks. Rain of loose papers settling.

EWAN: Give me the address list.

MARA: No.

EWAN: I will visit every family tonight.

MARA: You will return to London on the mail coach. Bell paid for your seat.

EWAN: Then I will miss it.

MARA: Your case is already loaded. The driver has orders not to wait.

EWAN: How many names did you take?

SFX: Mara closes the deposit ledger.

MARA: Seventy settlers have paid deposits.

EWAN: When are they meant to sail?

MARA: Their ship is scheduled to sail tomorrow morning—before you can warn them.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Bell publicly blamed Ewan for a damaged Ravenshore bond and dismissed his explanation in front of investors.

state_changes.fact: His professional competence was publicly discredited.
He established authority over Ewan before the investors.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Macrae received public applause after claiming Ravenshore's land and future revenue would support the bond issue.

state_changes.fact: His public credibility with Bell's investors increased.
Investor enthusiasm increased despite the defective certificate.

beat_sheet.location: Bond records room beneath Bell's salon
beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan and Pippa found that serial R-4187 on Miles's bond had already been assigned to a different investor who paid in full.

state_changes.fact: He obtained evidence that the bond problem was not merely a printing defect.
One certificate serial was confirmed as sold to two investors.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Bell opened his private ledger, and Ewan found serial R-4187 entered twice in different ink on dates eleven days apart.

state_changes.fact: He confirmed the duplicate serial in Bell's private records.
His private ledger connected his office to both payments.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Bell refused to cancel the duplicate bond, invoked Ewan's family debts, and ordered him to recreate a water-damaged register.

state_changes.fact: His mother's financial vulnerability was used to pressure him into compliance.
He refused to correct the duplicated bond entry.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Bell locked Ewan inside the counting room until he recreated all 312 entries in the missing bond register.

state_changes.fact: He was confined and forced to reconstruct the bond register overnight.
Its 312 entries were scheduled for reconstruction by Ewan.

beat_sheet.location: Route from the Ravenshore office to Alderwick Auction Rooms
beat_sheet.what_happened: Six sealed cases containing 800 Ravenshore certificates authenticated with forged Ewan initials were transported to the auction house.

state_changes.fact: Eight hundred certificates bearing forged Ewan initials entered auction-house custody.
His identity was attached to certificates he did not authenticate.

beat_sheet.note: The dispatch occurs away from the cast and establishes deliberate open canon before Pippa obtains the freight docket.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Pippa passed Ewan a freight docket proving that a fresh shipment had reached the auction house with his forged initials on every certificate.

state_changes.fact: He learned his forged initials appeared on 800 auction certificates.
She shared evidence of the unauthorized shipment with Ewan.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Mara publicly presented Ewan as a Ravenshore government clerk and required him to answer prospective settlers' questions.

state_changes.fact: His clerical role was used as public evidence of Ravenshore's legitimacy.
She gained an official-looking witness for the recruiting meeting.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan admitted that he had never seen Ravenshore's wages, farms, capital, harbour, bank, or completed surveys, while Mara reframed his answers as support for settlement.

state_changes.fact: She learned Ewan had seen official papers but not the advertised country.
He identified the lack of firsthand surveying evidence.
His careful qualifications were publicly converted into apparent endorsement.

beat_sheet.location: Deposit table in Calderwick recruiting hall
beat_sheet.what_happened: Agnes paid seventeen pounds for thirty acres and three berths, and Ewan wrote her entry into the deposit ledger.

state_changes.fact: She committed seventeen pounds of her family's shop proceeds to Ravenshore land and passage.
His handwriting became the recorded witness to Agnes's purchase.
She secured Agnes's family deposit.

beat_sheet.location: Calderwick recruiting hall after the meeting
beat_sheet.what_happened: Mara revealed that seventy settlers had paid deposits and their ship was scheduled to sail the next morning before Ewan could warn them.

state_changes.fact: Seventy paid settlers were committed to a departure on 1822-09-25.
He lacked enough time to warn the paid settlers before departure.
She completed recruitment for the scheduled sailing.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: whether the repeated bond serial was an accidental misprint or was also recorded inside Bell's accounts
promise_ledger.how_paid: Ewan found serial R-4187 entered twice in Bell's private ledger in different ink on dates eleven days apart.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: whether the auction shipment bearing Ewan's forged initials will be sold to investors
whether Ewan can warn the seventy settlers and what they will find after sailing

dates_fixed.what: Bell's London investor salon and Ewan's discovery of the duplicate serial
Bell confines Ewan overnight while the auction shipment is dispatched
The Calderwick recruiting meeting takes final deposits
The seventy settlers' ship is scheduled to sail
